title: Robust embed cache canonical IDs and graceful staleness protocol
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: The current embedding cache sees high churn and misses for small textual variants (punctuation, casing, whitespace, trailing context) and near-duplicates across tenants. This increases embedding compute, increases tail latency for reranking endpoints, and causes higher unit cost. Existing approaches partially dedupe by exact content hash or tenant coalescing but fail across natural text variants and short prefixes used by autocomplete/rerank flows.

Goal: Implement a canonical ID scheme plus a lease-based graceful staleness protocol that: (1) maps semantically equivalent inputs to the same cache keys where safe, (2) preserves per-tenant isolation and privacy guarantees, (3) ensures eventual correctness via leases/fallbacks to avoid stale results, and (4) provides observability and rollback knobs. Target improvements: 20-35% cache hit increase for production reranking workloads, 5-12% median latency reduction under normal load, and 18-30% fewer compute tokens billed in embedded-heavy routes.

Design highlights: 1) Canonicalization pipeline produces a deterministic canonical_id plus lightweight variant_fingerprint. Steps: unicode normalization (NFKC), lowercasing, aggressive whitespace and punctuation normalization, strip boilerplate stopphrases for known product flows, token-length bucketing for short inputs, and a final locality-sensitive hashing (LSH) pass tuned to avoid over-merge. Canonical_id is the deterministic string key; variant_fingerprint is short fixed-length fingerprint stored with each cache entry for audit and selective revalidation.

2) Lease-based staleness protocol: cache entries are stored with a lease TTL and a grace window. On lease expiration the entry moves into GRACE state where a single background worker performs revalidation (compute fresh embedding and compare variant_fingerprint). Reads during GRACE can still return the old vector with a special observability tag; if revalidation fails similarity thresholds we evict and recompute synchronously for the next reader. This reduces thundering herd and avoids returning obviously stale deduped vectors after content drift.

3) Tenant-aware safety: canonicalization rules are configurable per-tenant. Default safe set applies broad normalization; high-security tenants can opt into strict mode (no punctuation stripping, exact-match fallbacks) enforced by tenant policy in the cache config. All canonicalization decisions are logged and explainable via the console audit.

4) Migration and co-existence: the new keys are namespaced under v2-canonical/ so both v1 exact-hash and v2 canonical entries can coexist. We’ll include a background backfill job that scans hot v1 keys and migrates to canonical keys where variant_fingerprint indicates equality.

5) Observability and metrics: new metrics (canonical_hit_rate, grace_reads, revalidation_fail_rate, dedupe_save_tokens) and per-route histograms. Sampling of inputs and canonicalization diffs will be stored for 30d for analysis.

Trade-offs and safety: Conservative defaults aim to prioritize recall/quality over maximal dedupe. LSH and stopphrase rules have tunable thresholds per project. The lease + revalidation reduces risk of returning semantically divergent cached vectors.

Testing & validation: offline bucketed A/B tests (recall@1/3/5, MRR, rerank latency distribution), synthetic mutation tests (punctuation/case/stopword variations), and canary rollout to 10% of traffic with forced revalidation logging.

Deliverables: API and runtime changes to cache keying, background revalidator, tenant config knobs, console observability, migration job, and an operator runbook.

migration_steps: 1) Add v2-canonical key namespace to cache schema and rollout in read path (no writes).
2) Enable canonicalization for 0% traffic and log diffs between v1 and v2 keys.
3) Start background hot-key scanner to create v2 entries for stable v1 keys.
4) Enable write-through to both v1 and v2 for a 2-week overlap period.
5) Enable lease protocol and GRACE reads for 10% traffic; monitor revalidation_fail_rate.
6) If metrics stable, increase traffic to 50% then 100%; finally retire hot-path v1 keys after 30d of parity.
metrics_targets: canonical_hit_rate >= 0.25 on rerank routes by week 4
median latency improvement >= 5% on p50 and p90 not regressing on p99
rollout_plan: Week 1: internal testing and agreement on normalization rules; deploy v2 read-only keying
Week 2: enable background backfill and sampling logging; run offline A/B tests
Week 3: enable write-through and lease protocol for 10% canary; monitor metrics hour-by-hour
Week 4: expand to 50% if canary stable; start tenant opt-in documentation
Week 5+: full rollout and v1 retirement window
